name: Monument Pipeline

values.EndLocation: Houston Ship Channel and Galveston County (La Porte, League City)

researcher_notes: Monument Pipeline is a real operating Texas intrastate gas transmission system of about 225 miles. It starts at the Katy hub, runs through Sugar Land to the Houston Ship Channel and into Galveston County. Trade press describes 16-inch lines and take-or-pay contracts with utilities, LNG shippers and industrial users, so it is transmission and storage, not retail distribution. It is a separate system from the Houston Pipeline System (P0203, now Energy Transfer) and from the Tejas Gas Pipeline (P0258). No existing row names Monument. Kinder Morgan agreed in April 2026 to buy it from ARM Energy Holdings for 505 million dollars. Its 10-Q for the quarter ended June 2026 reports the purchase closed May 1, 2026. Earlier owner was NextEra Energy Partners. Capacity of 285,000 Mcf per day appears in the Pipeline and Gas Journal article (the number 285 was found on the page; the exact phrasing was not read in full). Diameter is blank because only some 16-inch lines are named. Texas Railroad Commission filings were not checked. Route not researched: no official GIS found, so RouteType unavailable. Owner is the exact gazetteer spelling Kinder Morgan Inc. Length 225 mi is the whole system, which exceeds the 25 km threshold. Status is operating, so this is an addition of a missing existing line rather than a proposed project.
